parsed.why: Most Protective tier: no facility ban, gender-identity anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage, care shield law, self-ID markers, no police targeting. Still under the hostile federal passport, entry-screening, facility and custody regime, which caps the score.

Only state criminalising trans restroom use in all public-facing private businesses — gas stations, restaurants, hospitals — first offence up to a year jail; suit pending, remedy not operating. Broadest universal-exposure criminal statute in the set.

Bathroom law enforced within days by troopers checking IDs at the capitol, plus fines and a top 'Do Not Travel' tier; definition act erases markers; worst recorded trans killings. Federal regime compounds it.

Facility restriction via K-12 ban and a binary-sex order reaching state-owned buildings, shelters and prisons; public-facility adult care ban with criminal penalties; no gender-identity hate-crime or anti-discrimination. No private-business bathroom crime.

Repealed its bathroom law and no facility bar or criminalisation is in force, but hate-crime and anti-discrimination coverage absent, original-sex display required on amended certificates, and bathroom bills revived. Near the national line.
